scope: Corollary 6.6 (Accuracy without increasing dependency depth) of the manuscript “Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling” (preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 139 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e9a41553023f95e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix J ≥ 1. In all the probability, harmonic, and centering integrations above, one may take at most N = ⌈10(J + 2)⌉ Picard layers. After any fixed w ∈ (0, t) is chosen, a common fixed interpolation order satisfying w(m − 3) > J + 10, t(m − 3) > J + 10, m > 4(J + 10) (6.17) suffices for the following conclusions, for all sufficiently large d. Probability transport from its exact starting marginal has endpoint RMS error at most polylog(d)δJ D; the same holds after division by an endpoint parameter bounded away from zero. The mean circuit with ideal anchors has RMS error at most polylog(d)σδJ D relative to (5.4). The number of layers of exact mean dependencies within either circuit is O((N + 1)2), inde- pendently of m, w, and the number of mesh cells. All mesh nodes, interpolation weights, scalar parameters, and iteration counts are deterministic functions of the prescribed parameters and dimension.
